'''Zcash''' is a privacy-focused [[cryptocurrency]] which features an encrypted ledger using [[zero-knowledge proof]]s.<ref name="Carlisle">{{Cite book |last=Carlisle |first=David |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qw3jEAAAQBAJ |title=The Crypto Launderers: Crime and Cryptocurrencies from the Dark Web to DeFi and Beyond |date=2023-12-26 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-1-394-20319-2 |page=70 |language=en}}</ref>

Launched in October 2016, Zcash was developed by cryptographers at [[Johns Hopkins University]] and [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] and derived its code from [[bitcoin]].<ref name="NYT">{{Cite news |last=Popper |first=Nathaniel |date=2016-10-31 |title=Zcash, a Harder-to-Trace Virtual Currency, Generates Price Frenzy |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/11/01/business/dealbook/zcash-a-harder-to-trace-virtual-currency-generates-price-frenzy.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190111120448/https://www.nytimes.com/2016/11/01/business/dealbook/zcash-a-harder-to-trace-virtual-currency-generates-price-frenzy.html |archive-date=11 January 2019 |access-date=26 January 2017 |work=The New York Times}}</ref><ref name="Hackett_Fortune_Oct2016">{{cite news |last1=Hackett |first1=Robert |title=Meet the Latest Hyped Cryptocurrency |url=https://fortune.com/2016/10/29/zcash-bitcoin-cryptocurrency/ |access-date=14 June 2026 |work=Fortune |date=29 October 2016 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Orcutt |first=Mike |date=2017-11-09 |title=A Mind-Bending Cryptographic Trick Promises to Take Blockchains Mainstream |url=https://www.technologyreview.com/2017/11/09/67587/a-mind-bending-cryptographic-trick-promises-to-take-blockchains-mainstream/ |website=MIT Technology Review}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Andy |date=2016-01-20 |title=Zcash, an Untraceable Bitcoin Alternative, Launches in Alpha |url=https://www.wired.com/2016/01/zcash-an-untraceable-bitcoin-alternative-launches-in-alpha/ |website=WIRED}}</ref> Zcash was one of the first large-scale implementations of zero-knowledge proofs outside of academia.<ref name="Fortune_ZKP">{{Cite news |last=Weiss |first=Ben |date=2023-06-05 |title=A brief history of zero-knowledge proofs, the buzzy mathematical technique that's taken crypto by storm |url=https://fortune.com/crypto/2023/06/05/zero-knowledge-proofs-history-zk-rollups-cryptography-zcash/ |access-date=22 March 2026 |work=Fortune |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name="IEEE_Ceremony">{{Cite web |last=Peck |first=Morgen E. |date=2016-12-02 |title=The Crazy Security Behind the Birth of Zcash, the Inside Story |url=https://spectrum.ieee.org/the-crazy-security-behind-the-birth-of-zcash |website=IEEE Spectrum}}</ref><ref name="Economist2016">{{Cite news |date=2016-10-27 |title=Known unknown |work=[[The Economist]] |url=https://www.economist.com/finance-and-economics/2016/10/27/known-unknown |accessdate=14 June 2026 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Design ==

Zcash is modeled on [[bitcoin]], sharing its [[proof-of-work]] consensus mechanism.<ref name="NYT" /><ref name="OuNov2016">{{cite web |last1=Elaine |first1=Ou |title=Bitcoin Isn't Anonymous Enough |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/opinion/articles/2016-11-01/bitcoin-isn-t-anonymous-enough?sref=UsAjUhBb |website=Bloomberg.com |publisher=Bloomberg |access-date=17 November 2020 |date=November 1, 2016 }}</ref><ref name="Orcutt_JPM">{{Cite web |last=Orcutt |first=Mike |date=2017-11-24 |title=Why America's Biggest Bank Digs Anonymous Cryptocurrency |url=https://www.technologyreview.com/2017/11/24/148040/why-americas-biggest-bank-digs-anonymous-cryptocurrency/ |website=MIT Technology Review}}</ref><ref name="Economist2016" /> 

In 2016, Tom Robinson, co-founder of blockchain tracing firm [[Elliptic (company)|Elliptic]], told [[CNBC]] that Zcash appeared to have achieved a high level of anonymity.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Graham |first=Luke |date=2016-10-31 |title=New bitcoin rival promises anonymity for online purchases |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2016/10/31/new-bitcoin-rival-zcash-promises-anonymity-for-online-purchases.html |website=CNBC}}</ref> 

Zcash supports two types of addresses: transparent addresses, which function similarly to bitcoin addresses with publicly visible transactions, and shielded addresses, which use zero-knowledge proofs to encrypt transaction data.<ref name="NYT" /><ref name="RAND">{{Cite web |last1=Silfversten |first1=Erik |last2=Favaro |first2=Marina |last3=Slapakova |first3=Linda |last4=Ishikawa |first4=Sascha |last5=Liu |first5=James |last6=Salas |first6=Adrian |date=2020-05-06 |title=Exploring the use of Zcash cryptocurrency for illicit or criminal purposes |url=https://www.rand.org/pubs/research_reports/RR4418.html |language=en |access-date=5 September 2020 |archive-date=21 September 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200921065603/https://www.rand.org/pubs/research_reports/RR4418.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="OuNov2016" /> Shielded transactions can be verified as valid without revealing the sender, recipient, or amount transferred.<ref name="Hackett_Fortune_Oct2016" /><ref name="OuNov2016" /> Users can transact between the two types, allowing funds to move between the transparent and shielded pools.<ref name="NYT" /> 

This optional privacy model is intended to preserve [[fungibility]], allowing units of the currency to be treated equally regardless of their transaction history.<ref name="OuNov2016" /><ref name="Hackett_Fortune_Oct2016" /> Users also have the option to share private viewing keys, allowing designated third parties to see their transaction details for auditing purposes.<ref name="OuNov2016" /><ref name="IEEE_Launch">{{Cite web |last=Peck |first=Morgen E. |date=2016-11-18 |title=A Blockchain Currency That Beats Bitcoin On Privacy |url=https://spectrum.ieee.org/a-blockchain-currency-that-beats-bitcoin-on-privacy |website=IEEE Spectrum}}</ref> A 2018 study found that while it is possible to use Zcash privately, the anonymity set of the shielded pool could be reduced through heuristics-based analysis of usage patterns.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last1=Kappos |first1=George |last2=Yousaf |first2=Haaroon |last3=Maller |first3=Mary |last4=Meiklejohn |first4=Sarah |date=2018 |title=An Empirical Analysis of Anonymity in Zcash |url=https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity18/presentation/kappos |language=en |pages=463–477 |isbn=978-1-939133-04-5 |access-date=17 April 2020 |archive-date=26 April 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200426184117/https://www.usenix.org/conference/usenixsecurity18/presentation/kappos |url-status=live }}</ref> The analysis predates subsequent protocol upgrades to the shielded transaction system.<ref name="Fortune_ZKP"/> 

In 2022, journalist [[Andy Greenberg]] described Zcash's shielded transactions as "provably inaccessible" to surveillance and said he had not seen evidence that its anonymity could be compromised.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Greenberg |first=Andy |date=2022 |title=Tracers in the Dark: The Global Hunt for the Crime Lords of Cryptocurrency |publisher=Doubleday |isbn=978-0-385-54809-0}}</ref>{{Page needed|date=May 2026}}

== History ==
Development work on Zcash began in 2013 by [[Johns Hopkins University]] professor [[Matthew D. Green|Matthew Green]] and his graduate students Ian Miers and Christina Garman, who developed the [[Zerocoin protocol]]. They subsequently joined forces with a team of cryptographers including [[Alessandro Chiesa]] and Madars Virza from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], and [[Eli Ben-Sasson]] from the [[Technion]] and [[Eran Tromer]] from [[Tel Aviv University]], who had developed a more efficient variant called zk-SNARKs.<ref name="NYT"/><ref name="Fortune_Dec2017">{{cite news |last1=Hackett |first1=Robert |title=Can This Man Build a Better Bitcoin? |url=https://fortune.com/2017/12/18/jp-morgan-bitcoin-zcash-wilcox/ |access-date=14 June 2026 |work=Fortune |date=18 December 2018 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Fortune_ZKP" /><ref name="IEEE_Launch"/> The development was completed by the for-profit Zcash Company, led by [[Zooko Wilcox-O'Hearn|Zooko Wilcox]], a [[Colorado]] based computer security specialist.<ref name="NYT"/> The Zcash Company raised over $3 million from investors including [[Naval Ravikant]].<ref name="NYT"/><ref name="Fortune_Dec2017"/>

Zcash was first mined in late October 2016.<ref name="OuNov2016"/> To generate revenue, 10% of all coins mined for the first four years were automatically distributed to the Zcash Company and the Zcash Foundation.<ref name="NYT"/>

The instantiation of the Zcash network required the creation of a master [[private key]]. To ensure privacy, this private key must later be destroyed, otherwise counterfeit Zcash coins could be generated. To maximize the chance that no one person could obtain the private key, software was written which allowed individuals from six different locations to collaboratively generate the private key, use it to instantiate Zcash, and then destroy the computers used in the process afterwards.<ref name="npr20210225">{{cite news |title=The Ceremony |url=https://www.wnycstudios.org/podcasts/radiolab/articles/ceremony |last1=Webster |first1=Molly |last2=Kielty |first2=Matt |work=[[Radiolab]] |publisher=[[National Public Radio]] |date=25 February 2021 |access-date=29 June 2021 |archive-date=28 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210628223502/https://www.wnycstudios.org/podcasts/radiolab/articles/ceremony |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Fortune_Dec2017" /><ref name="IEEE_Ceremony"/> In 2019, Electric Coin Company researcher Sean Bowe discovered Halo, a technique for generating zero-knowledge proofs without requiring a trusted setup ceremony.<ref name="Fortune_ZKP" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bowe |first1=Sean |last2=Grigg |first2=Jack |last3=Hopwood |first3=Daira |date=2019 |title=Recursive Proof Composition without a Trusted Setup |url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2019/1021 |journal=Cryptology ePrint Archive}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hackett |first=Robert |date=2019-02-05 |title=Zcash Discloses Vulnerability That Could Have Allowed 'Infinite Counterfeit' Cryptocurrency |url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/zcash-discloses-vulnerability-could-allowed-160044323.html |work=Fortune |via=Yahoo News |access-date=14 June 2026}}</ref> This eliminated the need for the elaborate multi-party ceremonies used at launch.

In 2018, ''[[MIT Technology Review]]'' named Zcash co-founder [[Alessandro Chiesa]], an assistant professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], to its [[Innovators Under 35]] list for his work on the zero-knowledge proof technology underlying the cryptocurrency.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Solomon |first=Dan |date=2018-06-27 |title=Alessandro Chiesa |url=https://www.technologyreview.com/innovator/alessandro-chiesa/ |website=MIT Technology Review}}</ref>

In 2022, [[Edward Snowden]] revealed that he had participated in the creation of Zcash under the pseudonym "John Dobbertin."<ref name="Snowden_Fortune">{{Cite web |last=Locke |first=Taylor |date=2022-04-28 |title=Edward Snowden says he's the mystery man involved in the creation of leading privacy cryptocurrency Zcash |url=https://fortune.com/crypto/2022/04/28/edward-snowden-crypto-zcash/ |access-date=2022-11-02 |website=Fortune |language=en |archive-date=2 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221102060005/https://fortune.com/crypto/2022/04/28/edward-snowden-crypto-zcash/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=del Castillo |first=Michael |date=2022-04-27 |title=Edward Snowden Revealed As Key Participant In Mysterious Ceremony Creating $2 Billion Anonymous Cryptocurrency |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/michaeldelcastillo/2022/04/27/edward-snowden-revealed-as-key-participant-in-mysterious-ceremony-creating-2-billion-anonymous-cryptocurrency/ |website=Forbes}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Christensen |first=Meg |date=2022-04-29 |title=Edward Snowden Taught Zcash CEO Zooko Wilcox A CIA Trick To Help Keep The Creation Ceremony Secure |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/megchristensen/2022/04/29/edward-snowden-taught-zcash-ceo-zooko-wilcox-a-cia-trick-to-help-keep-the-creation-ceremony-secure/ |website=Forbes}}</ref> Other participants in the ceremony included [[Peter Todd (programmer)|Peter Todd]], a [[Bitcoin Core]] developer.<ref name="Snowden_Fortune" />

On February 21, 2019, the "Zcash Company" announced a rebranding as the Electric Coin Company (ECC).<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |date=2019-02-21 |title=Goodbye, Zcash Company. Hello, Electric Coin Company. |url=https://electriccoin.co/zh/blog/goodbye-zcash-company-hello-electric-coin-company/ |access-date=2020-11-09 |website=Electric Coin Company |language=en-US |archive-date=21 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021201008/https://electriccoin.co/zh/blog/goodbye-zcash-company-hello-electric-coin-company/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2020, the Electric Coin Company transitioned to nonprofit ownership, becoming a wholly owned subsidiary of the Bootstrap Project, a [[501(c)(3) organization]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-10-27 |title=ECC owners approve donation to Bootstrap Project |url=https://electriccoin.co/blog/ecc-owners-approve-donation-to-bootstrap-project/ |access-date=2020-11-09 |website=Electric Coin Company |language=en-US |archive-date=9 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109165654/https://electriccoin.co/blog/ecc-owners-approve-donation-to-bootstrap-project/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In September 2023, a mining pool named ViaBTC had seized control of over half the hashing power on Zcash. This 51% dominance raised worries about a [[Double-spending|51% attack]], where they could potentially manipulate transactions and harm the network. In response, Coinbase placed Zcash markets into "limit-only" mode in an effort to prevent significant price swings.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-09-26 |title=Crypto and the Curse of the 51% |language=en |work=Bloomberg.com |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/newsletters/2023-09-26/zcash-blockchain-viabtc-mining-pool-concentration-shows-51-attack-risks |access-date=2023-12-24 |archive-date=27 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230927184355/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/newsletters/2023-09-26/zcash-blockchain-viabtc-mining-pool-concentration-shows-51-attack-risks |url-status=live }}</ref>

In November 2025, [[Cameron Winklevoss]] and [[Tyler Winklevoss]] invested $50 million to launch Cypherpunk Technologies, a digital-asset treasury company focused on the cryptocurrency.<ref name="WSJ_2026"/>

In January 2026, the [[U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission]] closed a probe into Zcash.<ref name="WSJ_2026">{{Cite news |last1=Zuckerman |first1=Gregory |last2=Huang |first2=Vicky Ge |date=2026-05-14 |title=It’s a More Secret Version of Bitcoin and It’s on a Tear |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |url=https://www.wsj.com/finance/currencies/zcash-crypto-winklevoss-78d71d51}}</ref>

In April 2026, Foundry, one of the largest [[bitcoin]] mining pool operators, launched a dedicated Zcash mining pool.<ref name="Fortune_Foundry">{{Cite news |last=Roberts |first=Jeff John |date=2026-04-13 |title=Bitcoin mining giant Foundry adds new pool for privacy-focused Zcash |url=https://fortune.com/2026/04/13/bitcoin-mining-giant-foundry-adds-new-pool-for-privacy-focused-zcash/ |work=[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]] |access-date=21 April 2026}}</ref>

== Usage ==

In 2017, [[JPMorgan Chase]] integrated Zcash's zero-knowledge proof technology into its enterprise blockchain platform Quorum to enable confidential transactions for business clients.<ref name="Fortune_Dec2017" /><ref name="Orcutt_JPM" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Hackett |first=Robert |date=2018-05-24 |title=How JPMorgan Chase Learned to Love the Blockchain |url=https://fortune.com/longform/jpmorgan-chase-tech-blockchain/ |access-date=4 May 2026 |work=Fortune |url-access=subscription}}</ref> ''[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]]'' reported that Zcash's fundamental technology would be added to the [[Ethereum]] network.<ref name="Fortune_Dec2017"/>

In late 2017, [[Grayscale Investments]] launched a Zcash investment fund, which is the company's third dedicated cryptocurrency fund after bitcoin and Ethereum Classic.<ref name="Hackett_Grayscale">{{Cite web |last=Hackett |first=Robert |date=2018-01-31 |title=One of Bitcoin's Biggest Asset Managers Says Zcash Could Hit $60,000 in 2025 |url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/one-bitcoin-biggest-asset-managers-153152018.html |work=Fortune |via=Yahoo News |access-date=4 May 2026}}</ref> In 2026, Grayscale filed with regulators to convert the fund into an [[exchange-traded fund]].<ref name="WSJ_2026"/>

In May 2018, the [[New York State Department of Financial Services]] approved Zcash for trading on [[Gemini (cryptocurrency exchange)|Gemini]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kharif |first=Olga |date=2018-05-14 |title='Privacy Coin' ZCash Lands on Winklevoss's Gemini Exchange |work=Bloomberg.com |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-05-14/gemini-gives-boost-to-privacy-coin-zcash-as-exchange-expands |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Shen |first=Lucinda |date=2018-05-15 |title=Here's Why Cryptocurrency Zcash Is Soaring While Bitcoin Languishes |url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/why-cryptocurrency-zcash-soaring-while-174720092.html |work=Fortune |via=Yahoo News |access-date=4 May 2026}}</ref>

The [[Freedom of the Press Foundation]], the [[Human Rights Foundation]], and the [[Electronic Frontier Foundation]] have accepted Zcash donations.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Liao |first=Shannon |date=2018-06-18 |title=The Freedom of the Press Foundation now accepts bitcoin cash, ether, and other cryptocurrencies |url=https://www.theverge.com/2018/6/18/17475318/freedom-press-foundation-cryptocurrency-bitcoin-ether-zcash |website=The Verge}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=del Castillo |first=Michael |date=2020-05-06 |title=Cypherpunk Zooko Wilcox Aims To Bring Anonymous Zcash To Law-Abiding Masses |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/michaeldelcastillo/2020/05/06/cypherpunk-zooko-wilcox-wants-zcash-mainstream/ |website=Forbes}}</ref>

=== Crime ===

In 2017, the European Union's law enforcement agency [[Europol]] flagged Zcash, along with bitcoin and [[Monero (cryptocurrency)|Monero]], for potential use in internet-based crime.<ref name="Bloomberg_Criminal">{{Cite news |last=Kharif |first=Olga |date=2018-01-02 |title=The Criminal Underworld Is Dropping Bitcoin for Another Currency |work=Bloomberg.com |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-01-02/criminal-underworld-is-dropping-bitcoin-for-another-currency}}</ref> The same report noted that Zcash was not known to have a significant criminal following.<ref name="Bloomberg_Criminal"/> In 2018, several Japanese exchanges delisted Zcash and other privacy-focused cryptocurrencies citing regulatory pressure following a major exchange hack; the delisted coins had not been involved in the hack.<ref name="DelCastillo_Japan">{{Cite web |last=del Castillo |first=Michael |date=2020-05-12 |title=Privacy Coins Monero, Zcash And Dash Face Uphill Battle In Japan |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/michaeldelcastillo/2020/05/12/privacy-coins-monero-zcash-and-dash-face-uphill-battle-in-japan/ |website=Forbes}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Evans |first=Jon |date=2018-06-24 |title=Zcash: life on the crypto roller coaster |url=https://techcrunch.com/2018/06/24/zcash-life-on-the-crypto-roller-coaster/ |website=TechCrunch}}</ref>

A 2020 research report by the [[RAND Corporation]] examined eight major [[dark web]] marketplaces and found that 59% of cryptocurrency mentions were bitcoin and 27% were [[Monero (cryptocurrency)|Monero]], compared with less than 1% for Zcash, concluding that there was "little evidence" that privacy coins were preferred by criminals despite their anonymity features.<ref name="RAND" /><ref name="DelCastillo_Japan" /> A 2023 analysis of cryptocurrency and crime similarly found that Zcash "featured very rarely on the dark web" compared to [[Monero (cryptocurrency)|Monero]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Carlisle |first=David |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qw3jEAAAQBAJ |title=The Crypto Launderers: Crime and Cryptocurrencies from the Dark Web to DeFi and Beyond |date=2023-12-26 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-1-394-20319-2 |pages=70–73 |language=en}}</ref>
